rv.q: Unfortunately, the inadequate production that surrounds it undermines both its message and its colorful characters.
Yet despite committed performances and relevant themes, the play ultimately feels more like an argument about activism than a piece of theater that fully dramatizes it.
Boehm’s play works best as a history lesson—a generation of young gay audiences may find enlightenment in those parts dealing with AIDS and ACT-UP—but it lacks the vitality of currency.

cn.t: Critics find this family drama about gay characters tackles familiar territory of substance-fueled conflict, drawing comparisons to classic American plays but ultimately landing as a mixed effort.
